movesets.name: Clangorous Soul
movesets.description:
Kommo-o is a decent late-game sweeper thanks to its access to Clangorous Soul, capable of cleaning weakened teams thanks to its combination of good bulk and serviceable typing to ease setup. Boomburst gives it a strong and no-drawback move to hit neutral foes, ranging from walls like Zapdos, Clefable, and Gliscor all the way to offensive ones like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W. Flamethrower provides Kommo-o with a way to threaten Gholdengo and other Steel-types like Corviknight and Iron Crown, preventing them from stopping its sweep. Clanging Scales can be used as a powerful STAB option that threatens Kommo-o's fellow Dragon-types like Kyurem, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite more easily while also being its most damaging move before Terastallizing, particularly against Ghost-types like Pecharunt, Dragapult, and Ceruledge. Drain Punch's healing can mitigate the health cost from Clangerous Soul while netting crucial KOs against Darkrai, Weavile, and Hisuian Samurott and denting special walls like Ting-Lu and Blissey, which wall it otherwise. Soundproof prevents Kommo-o from being forced to switch out and get its sweep stopped by Roar users such as Moltres and Zamazenta while also making it immune to Parting Shot from Pecharunt and Psychic Noise from Galarian Slowking and Iron Crown. Tera Normal is the go-to choice for boosting Boomburst's damage output while granting it a decent neutral typing against potential revenge killers like Enamorus and Weavile. A Naive nature alongside an EV spread of 4 Atk / 252 SpA / 252 Spe should only be used on Drain Punch variants.

Kommo-o fits best on offense teams that want to make use of its good bulk and resistances to allow it to set up and sweep or weaken the opposing team considerably for other sweepers, as well as being able to switch into certain threats in a pinch. Kingambit makes for a great offensive partner, as Kommo-o can soften or outright beat foes such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T to make way for a Kingambit sweep later. Furthermore, Kingambit can take care of Kommo-o's enemies such as Galarian Slowking, Garganacl, and Pecharunt or Blissey depending on Kommo-o's choice of STAB move. Scizor is also a great offensive partner, being able to pivot out and bring Kommo-o into the field safely while threatening Fairy-types and Ting-Lu. Ogerpon-W is a fantastic partner, as it can easily punch holes in bulkier teams and weaken them to enable a sweep from Kommo-o. Defensive teammates such as Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Primarina appreciate Kommo-o's ability to switch into Grass- and Water-type threats such as Hisuian Samurott and Rillaboom. In return, Great Tusk provides entry hazard control with Rapid Spin to keep Kommo-o healthy and threatens special walls such as Blissey, Galarian Slowking, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl. Landorus-T grants Kommo-o a way to get onto the field safely through U-turn, checks and weakens threats such as Zamazenta and Dragonite, and is capable of setting Stealth Rock, which guarantees that a boosted Kommo-o KOes Gliscor with Tera Normal Boomburst and Pecharunt with Clanging Scales. Hazard setters and removers in general are very appreciated, due to Kommo-o's recoil damage when boosting along with its nature as an all-or-nothing sweeper. Iron Treads is a great partner, as it can set up Stealth Rock, use Rapid Spin to get rid of hazards for Kommo-o, and switch into Fairy-types such as Hatterene, Clefable, and special variants of Iron Valiant. Ting-Lu is also a phenomenal teammate, as Kommo-o covers Pokemon that threaten it such as Hisuian Samurott, Ogerpon-W, and Rillaboom, while Ting-Lu can set up Stealth Rock or Spikes and phaze problematic Pokemon such as Calm Mind Raging Bolt. Sticky Web users such as Araquanid and Ribombee can prove to be very useful teammates for Kommo-o as well, crippling threats like Booster Energy Iron Valiant, Choice Scarf Darkrai, and Meowscarada. Alomomola is a good fit for less offensive teams, being able to both keep Kommo-o healthy with Wish and bring it to the field safely with Flip Turn, while Kommo-o handles Ogerpon-W. Alolan Ninetales is a terrific partner as well, being able to set up Aurora Veil, enhancing Kommo-o's bulk further and allowing it to set up more safely. Alolan Ninetales also helps Kommo-o defensively by switching in on Ice-type threats like Weavile and Kyurem.

strategies.comments:
Other Options

Dragon (Choice Specs)

Focus Blast can be considered over Aura Sphere due to its obscene damage, which prevents Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu from tanking any additional hits while 2HKOing Mandibuzz and Blissey. However, Focus Blast's accuracy makes it a less reliable option than Aura Sphere.

movesets.name: Mixed Wallbreaker (Dragon)
movesets.description:
With its decent mixed offensive prowess, Kommo-o can use a mixed set with Close Combat to put more pressure on the defensive cores of opposing Steel, Dark, and Dragon teams. Close Combat pulverizes Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, Ting-Lu, and Empoleon that otherwise can try and scout other Kommo-o sets. Close Combat also deals with Scrafty, which is troublesome for most Dragon teams. Clanging Scales punishes switch-ins like Dragapult, Sableye, and Archaludon, 2HKOing the last two defensive walls. Flamethrower deals with Steel team's switch-ins in Skarmory and Gholdengo. Vacuum Wave picks off faster threats like Meowscarada and Greninja. 92 Atk EVs coupled with Expert Belt ensures Kommo-o OHKOes Hisuian Goodra with Close Combat. A Rash nature is preferred, as it lets Kommo-o 2HKO non-specially defensive Gholdengo with Flamethrower and reduces the prior damage needed for Vacuum Wave to KO Hisuian Samurott and Greninja late-game.

Mixed Kommo-o struggles with bulkier defensive cores such as those of Flying and Water teams, and it is unable to 2HKO specially defensive Corviknight, so wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Latios make for great teammates. Dragapult also deals with faster threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and loves Kommo-o's ability to punch through special walls like Ting-Lu and Hisuian Goodra. Latios deals with Poison-types like Clodsire and pressures Flying and Fighting teams. It can even run Flip Turn if using a Choice Scarf to pivot Kommo-o in against Ting-Lu, Empoleon, and Gholdengo, all of which check Latios. Both of them appreciate Kommo-o's ability in Bulletproof, as it covers for their weakness to Shadow Ball. Kyurem and Raging Bolt devastate the defensive cores of Water and Flying teams and love Kommo-o's ability to remove their checks in Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Empoleon. Kyurem deals with Clodsire, while Raging Bolt zaps Corviknight and Toxapex for Kommo-o. Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon are notably not weak to any of Dragon's weaknesses, with Hisuian Goodra dealing with Primarina, Flutter Mane, and Greninja and Archaludon covering for physical threats like Roaring Moon and Meowscarada. Hisuian Goodra can also use Knock Off to remove items from walls, allowing Kommo-o to plausibly 2HKO specially defensive Corviknight after Stealth Rock. Archaludon also provides Stealth Rock, which help chip down speedy threats to the point where Kommo-o can safely remove them with Vacuum Wave. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon deals with faster threats like non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and Flutter Mane, and it also pivots Kommo-o in against walls like Skarmory. Swords Dance Garchomp appreciates Kommo-o's ability to break down Steel and Dragon teams, which paves a way for Garchomp to sweep. It also deals with Volcarona and Articuno, which wall Kommo-o. Other setup sweepers like Dragonite benefit from Kommo-o breaking its checks in Skarmory and Archaludon.

movesets.name: Choice Specs (Dragon)
movesets.description:
Choice Specs Kommo-o is a great wallbreaker for Dragon teams thanks to its incredible STAB combination and access to Vacuum Wave, which allows it to force out problematic threats like Greninja and Darkrai. Clanging Scales complements Kommo-o's coverage, punishing switch-ins like Dragapult, Mandibuzz, and Toxapex that can shrug off its Fighting-type moves, and it also damages Substitute Spectrier and Volcarona. Flamethrower rounds out Kommo-o's coverage against Steel teams by roasting Gholdengo and Corviknight. Vacuum Wave lets Kommo-o pick off massive threats to Dragon teams like Meowscarada, Choice Band Excadrill, and Hisuian Samurott. Bulletproof lets it switch into and nullify Shadow Ball from Choice Specs Spectrier and Hisuian Zoroark. A Timid nature lets Kommo-o outspeed Jolly Mamoswine and damage it with Vacuum Wave before it can be picked off by Ice Shard, as well as allowing Kommo-o to outspeed and remove Dragonite and Adamant Lokix. Alternatively, a Modest nature enables Kommo-o to OHKO Greninja and Meowscarada with Vacuum Wave after Stealth Rock damage and guarantees a 2HKO on specially defensive Corviknight and Hisuian Goodra.

Both Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra help with Kommo-o's debilitating Fairy weakness by dealing with physical and special attackers, respectively: Archaludon deals with Azumarill and Mimikyu, which can use Kommo-o as a setup opportunity, while Hisuian Goodra can sponge attacks from the likes of Flutter Mane, Choice Specs Greninja, and Primarina. Archaludon also provides Stealth Rock support, a welcome tool to help Kommo-o break through and revenge kill foes. Both Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra can handle opposing Dragon-types as well; Archaludon can cover against Dragon Dance Dragapult, while Hisuian Goodra can handle Latios. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon appreciates Kommo-o's ability to threaten Steel-types that can take it on like Skarmory, and in return, it provides speed control, removing Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hoopa-U, which readily deal with Kommo-o. Dragapult can run a variety of sets from Choice Specs to further pressure special walls alongside Kommo-o, Choice Band to lure and weaken Hisuian Goodra and Clodsire, and status-spreading sets to slow down opposing teams. In return, Kommo-o overpowers Dark-types like Bisharp and Hisuian Samurott. Both Latios and Latias are great teammates, as they provide speed control and help in the Poison and Fighting matchups, two major struggles for Kommo-o. Latios can use an Expert Belt set to further pressure Water and Flying teams, while Latias also provides very helpful utility in the form of Healing Wish and Trick to render checks like Galarian Slowking much less potent. Garchomp can pack Spikes or Stone Edge to help Kommo-o's wallbreaking prowess or deal with Moltres and Volcarona for Dragon teams. In return, Kommo-o deals with Corviknight and Skarmory for Garchomp. Dragonite forms a priority core with Kommo-o and loves Kommo-o's ability to remove pesky Steel-types like Archaludon and Skarmory, allowing it to clean up Dragon and Flying teams late-game.

movesets.name: Clangorous Soul
movesets.description: • This EV Spread survives a Chien-Pao Ice Spinner and outspeeds Dragapult after Clangorous Soul.

strategies.overview:
• Kommo-o is a strong setup sweeper thanks to its excellent defensive stats and access to STAB Body Press. Its defensive typing gives it critical resistances to the signature moves of both Urshifu formes, which ignore the Defense boosts from Iron Defense. With proper support, Kommo-o is capable of becoming extremely difficult to remove once it starts setting up Iron Defense, making it an extremely effective sweeper.

  • Kommo-o appreciates teammates that help it set up more easily. Incineroar and Amoonguss are great at this, with Incineroar being able to cycle Fake Out and Parting Shot, while Amoonguss provides Spore as well as redirection support. Both give Kommo-o turns to set up and more room to maneuver, and they also have strong defensive synergy with Kommo-o. Ting-Lu is another great partner, as it can whittle down foes with Ruination, and its ability Vessel of Ruin makes Kommo-o harder to remove.

  • Ironically, one of Kommo-o's biggest weaknesses is its typing. While its numerous resistances are valuable, namely into the Ogerpon and Urshifu formes, in exchange, it is weak to a whole host of common offensive types. Strong attackers such as Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Chien-Pao hit Kommo-o for super effective damage, with the former two being special attackers and the latter using Sacred Sword, meaning they all ignore Iron Defense boosts. Kommo-o is often forced to Terastallize, and requires careful positioning around threats to conserve its HP for a late game sweep.

movesets.name: Iron Defense Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Iron Head is used to hit Flutter Mane, which is immune to Body Press.

  • Leftovers is used for extra recovery, since Kommo-o will be on the field for long periods of time.

  • Overcoat is picked for an immunity to powder moves, allowing it to ignore Amoonguss, which can otherwise redirect a resisted Body Press and slow it down with Spore.

  • The Special Defense investment allows Kommo-o to live a Blood Moon from Life Orb Ursaluna-B and makes Shadow Ball from Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane a 3HKO. On the physical side, the Defense investment allows Kommo-o to comfortably live Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, as well as making Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow a 3HKO after Terastallizing into Steel. The Attack investment gives the best chance for an OHKO on Flutter Mane with Iron Head after Terastallizing into Steel.

  • Tera Steel has the best synergy with Kommo-o's original typing since it provides resistances to every type that Kommo-o is weak to. It also gives STAB to Iron Head, allowing for a favorable roll to OHKO Flutter Mane

strategies.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Kommo-o greatly appreciates redirection from Pokemon like Electabuzz and Amoonguss, allowing it to safely set up. Electabuzz can also use Taunt to prevent Haze from removing Kommo-o's boosts. Damage reduction like Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp from Incineroar and Magmar can also aid Kommo-o in setting up. Aurora Veil and dual screens from Alolan Ninetales and Grimmsnarl, respectively, can also help in damage reduction. Fake Out and healing from Rillaboom and its Grassy Terrain are helpful in helping with safe setup and longevity, respectively.
  • Gholdengo is a good partner, as it threatens Fairy-types like Hatterene and Clefairy. Sneasler can also threaten Fairy-types with Dire Claw. Kingambit is another good offensive partner, threatening Ghost-types like Dragapult that would otherwise wall out Body Press Kommo-o sets. Tyranitar can threaten Flying-types like Dragonite and Talonflame.
  • Kommo-o can struggle immensely against Fairy-types like Primarina and Psychic-type spam teams that include Pokemon like Indeedee-M. Dragonite is another issue, dealing a lot of damage and using Haze to remove Kommo-o's boosts. Dragonite also has Multiscale, weakening Kommo-o's damage. Steel-types like Gholdengo threaten good damage into the Fairy-types, while Dark-types like Incineroar can easily take attacks like Expanding Force from Psychic-type spam teams. Allies like Porygon2 and Grimmsnarl can threaten Dragonite for good damage with Ice Beam and Spirit Break, respectively.

Strategy Comments

  • Kommo-o's main role is to get set up and sweep or clean up. Kommo-o works best when next to support that helps it set up like redirection and Fake Out.
  • Kommo-o works well as a cleaner during the late-game, so aiming to remove pieces that might stop it like Dragonite is helpful. Reserving support like Electabuzz for Kommo-o can also be helpful, as it helps Kommo-o set up.
  • Haze is a big issue for Kommo-o, punishing it for setting up. Fast and powerful attackers like Dragapult can deal major damage before Kommo-o sets up or attacks. Fast Taunt from foes like Maushold is a check to Kommo-o, that is, if you predict correctly whether or not Kommo-o sets up. Haze can be stopped by Taunt, and fast breakers or Taunt can be stopped by redirection from allies like Electabuzz.

movesets.name: Clangorous Soul
movesets.description:
• Clangorous Soul Kommo-o aims to set up and sweep or deal great amounts of damage to the majority of the metagame. It avoids Spore thanks to Overcoat or becomes immune to attacks like Hyper Voice thanks to Soundproof while enjoying the fact that there aren't that many Fairy-types in the format, allowing Clanging Scales to hit almost everything in the format for solid damage.
  • Clangorous Soul allows Kommo-o to set up, which can be aided with redirection. Clanging Scales can deal good spread damage while also boosting Kommo-o's Special Attack with Throat Spray if it hasn't used Clangorous Soul. Flamethrower can threaten Steel-types like Gholdengo that resist Clanging Scales while hitting hard into metagame threats like Rillaboom and Alolan Ninetales. Aura Sphere, on the other hand, is a good STAB option that also hits Steel-types, doing good damage into Pokemon like Archaludon and Kingambit.
  • Throat Spray's extra Special Attack boost in conjunction with Clangorous Soul allows Flamethrower to OHKO Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Alolan Ninetales or Aura Sphere to OHKO Tyranitar. Leftovers is good to heal back the damage dealt from Clangorous Soul, increasing its longevity.
  • Tera Fire grants a resistance to Fairy-type attacks and Make it Rain and gives Flamethrower a STAB boost. Tera Steel grants more defensive properties, letting it resist Dragon- and Flying-type attacks from Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Dragonite.
  • 188 Speed EVs let Kommo-o outspeed Pelipper while outpacing Sneasler after a Clangorous Soul. The Special Attack investment lets the first Kommo-o set OHKO Kingambit with +2 Flamethrower while also OHKOing Archaludon with Aura Sphere after the same boosts. The alternative EV spread outspeeds Rillaboom without any boosts while taking under 50% from Scale Shot from Dragonite when Terastallized into Fire.
  • Although Clangorous Soul sets are more destructive than Iron Defense sets, losing health early can lead to Kommo-o easily getting KOed by strong neutral attacks. Unlike Iron Defense, Clangorous Soul is not an easily spammable move and is really only used once per game.

movesets.name: Iron Defense
movesets.description:
• With Iron Defense, Kommo-o is able to set up and stay on the field for a long time, taking attacks from Pokemon like Sneasler and Rillaboom.
  • Iron Defense and Body Press are Iron Defense Kommo-o's main source of damage, hitting a lot of the metagame really well, like Porygon2 and Ursaluna-B.
  • Leftovers increases Kommo-o's longevity, making it incredibly difficult to remove.
  • The EVs are physically defensive to deal more damage with Body Press, OHKOing both Ursaluna formes after a Iron Defense. The Special Defense EVs let it survive a Life Orb-boosted Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B. The second EV spread can survive Tera Fire Choice Specs Eruption from Timid Hisuian Typhlosion.
  • Iron Defense Kommo-o is quite vulnerable to special attacks, with no way to boost its Special Defense. It can also be quite slow, so faster threats can remove Kommo-o before it gets boosts or disrupt Kommo-o, preventing set up.

strategies.outdated: This analysis is from before our transition to full analyses, and may contain outdated information.

movesets.name: Galvanize
movesets.description: Kommo-o finds a decent niche on offensive teams as a mixed attacker with strong coverage. Boomburst scares off walls such as Mandibuzz, Corviknight, and Manaphy. Clanging Scales threatens Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Pecharunt, while Close Combat notably allows Kommo-o to smack special walls like Blissey, Swampert, and Volt Absorb Empoleon attempting to check it. Stealth Rock synergizes well with Kommo-o's ability to scare away entry hazard removers like the aforementioned Mandibuzz and Corviknight. Clangorous Soul allows it to act as a passable setup sweeper instead, preventing threats like Roaring Moon and Iron Boulder from revenge killing it while increasing its offensive capabilities. Life Orb is typically preferred for its consistent damage boost, but Throat Spray can be used on Clangorous Soul sets to avoid recoil. Kommo-o's lack of longevity necessitates either teammates that can make up for its absent defensive utility like Corviknight and Manaphy or offensive teammates that can keep up the pressure like Iron Moth and Chien-Pao. Select revenge killers like Dragonite, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Azelf naturally outspeed Kommo-o even after a Clangorous Soul, so answers to them like Kingambit, Great Tusk, and Roaring Moon make for good partners. Kommo-o appreciates pivots like Azelf, Sandy Shocks, and Roaring Moon because they can pivot out on their checks like Blissey, Empoleon, and Corviknight and safely bring it in to start threatening the opposing team. Kommo-o greatly appreciates dual screens support from setters like Corviknight and Deoxys-S allowing it to have an easier time setting up with Clangorous Soul or supporting its teammates with Stealth Rock; alternatively, Sticky Web from Smeargle and Ribombee can help it outspeed Choice Scarf revenge killers like Latios, Azelf, and Roaring Moon after a Clangorous Soul.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 9-10 points

Tera Price Range: 11-12 points

Overview: Kommo-o is an extremely versatile Pokemon and strong attacker that takes advantage of an expansive movepool, usable mixed attacking stats, and various setup moves to sweep teams. With solid utility moves and good bulk, it can also serve as a defensive Pokemon. However, Kommo-o is slow and has a typing that leaves it vulnerable to a lot of common types, so it needs a lot of support to sweep teams.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Physical Setup Sweeper: With great physical coverage and reliable setup moves, Kommo-o can be a physical sweeper that takes advantage of the unpredictability of its set.

Special Setup Sweeper: Due to the interaction of Throat Spray + Clangorous Soul, Kommo-o can also be a special sweeper, once again taking advantage of the unpredictability of its set.

Defensive Utility: Using Body Press with its great physical bulk, Kommo-o can be a defensive Pokemon that can check numerous wallbreakers while still dishing out good damage.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, Body Press, Aura Sphere, Focus Blast, Vacuum Wave, Drain Punch, Low Kick, Scale Shot, Outrage, Dragon Claw, Draco Meteor, Clanging Scales

Setup Moves: Clangorous Soul, Dragon Dance, Belly Drum, Bulk Up, Iron Defense, Swords Dance

Utility Moves: Taunt, Roar, Dragon Tail, Stealth Rock, Substitute

Coverage: Boomburst, Earthquake, Fire Punch, Flamethrower, Flash Cannon, Ice Punch, Iron Head, Poison Jab, Rock Slide, Shadow Claw, Throat Chop, Thunder Punch, X-Scissor, Aerial Ace

Niche Moves

Metal Sound: If using a special Kommo-o set, Metal Sound can be used to activate Throat Spray while forcing the foe out, allowing Kommo-o to get a free attack off.

Endure: Endure is useful for both activating pinch Berries and getting additional Rocky Helmet damage.

Common Items

Throat Spray: Thanks to Clangorous Soul being a sound-based move, using it with Throat Spray allows Kommo-o to increase its Special Attack two stages. Kommo-o can alternatively use Clanging Scales or Boomburst to deal damage while still activating the Throat Spray.

Leftovers: Due to Kommo-o not having any reliable ways to recover health, Leftovers is important for keeping it healthy.

Salac / Sitrus Berry: Since both Clangorous Soul and Belly Drum cut Kommo-o's health, it is able to activate both Salac and Sitrus Berry by itself consistently. Thanks to Soundproof, it also does not have to worry about moves that get past Substitute for Belly Drum sets.

Lum Berry: Lum Berry allows Kommo-o to get around status spreaders, which would normally hinder its ability to set up.

Rocky Helmet: On defensive sets, Rocky Helmet is a great alternative if healing from Leftovers is not necessary.

Niche Items

Damage-boosting Items: Physical Kommo-o appreciates any boost in damage to its attacks it can get, and it certainly has a wide enough array of coverage to take advantage of a Choice Band. Providing more immediate power than Throat Spray would, Choice Specs can alternatively enable Kommo-o to take advantage of its powerful STAB moves on the special side, including Vacuum Wave to revenge kill, especially if your opponent is anticipating a physical Kommo-o.

Resistance Berries: Using Kommo-o's natural bulk, a resistance Berry can allow it to more freely set up on Pokemon that may have super effective coverage against it.

Eject Pack: With Clanging Scales and Draco Meteor, Kommo-o can use Eject Pack to get a powerful move off while pivoting away.

Loaded Dice: On Swords Dance sets especially, Loaded Dice Scale Shot can give Kommo-o a powerful attack that also gives a boost to its meager Speed.

Tera

Kommo-o is a pretty good Tera Captain in spite of its steep price. It is a Pokemon that has to be carefully built around as a Tera Captain, but it also allows for another high-value Tera Captain if picked. Most of its value comes from its versatility in set options that all benefit from Tera; for instance, it can use Tera Normal to give STAB to its Boomburst as well as shed its weaknesses, but it can really take advantage of pretty much any Tera type. Tera Steel, Poison, and Fire all turn Kommo-o's 4x weakness to Fairy into a resistance while boosting its strong moves with STAB and giving it immunity to poison or burn. Tera Electric is a generally neutral Tera type that prevents Kommo-o from being paralyzed and boosts Thunder Punch to hit the bulky Water- and Flying-types that may try to check Kommo-o. Finally, Tera Dragon and Fighting are usable options that boost Kommo-o's already-powerful STAB moves.

Draft Strategy

Kommo-o needs a lot of support and fits best on offense-oriented teams that enable it as a sweeper. It is slow and does not have a way to recover lost health outside of Rest and Drain Punch, and although it can be either offensive or defensive, it is generally relegated to the role of a late-game sweeper. It often has to be drafted with the knowledge you will not use it until a certain point in the game, so its intended role has to be drafted around craftily to make sure it is successful.

Speed Control: Even with a Speed boost, Kommo-o finds itself outsped by a lot of Pokemon. It benefits from being paired with faster teammates such as Iron Moth, Darkrai, and Greninja that can efficiently outrun its checks. Additionally, Sticky Web is usually a gimmick that is easy to work around, but even a cheap setter like Ariados or Cutiefly along with more consistent speed control helps Kommo-o a great deal.

Defensive Pivot: Kommo-o desperately needs something that can soak up the common moves it is weak to; slow Steel-types like Scizor and Empoleon can accomplish this while generating momentum with U-turn and Flip Turn, respectively.

Entry Hazard Control: Since Kommo-o often needs its foes to be weakened, an entry hazard setter such as Ting-Lu or Hisuian Samurott can accomplish this as the game goes on. On the other hand, Kommo-o can be weakened by opposing entry hazards, especially Toxic Spikes, so it's important to pair it with hazard removers such as Iron Treads and Glimmora.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Despite having access to both Poison- and Steel-type moves, Kommo-o already struggles with four-move syndrome, and Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Hatterene can deal significant damage to it with even a weak STAB move.

Mixed Walls: Even with the unpredictability Kommo-o brings, mixed walls like Toxapex and Scream Tail can tank both physical and special attacks and stop Kommo-o's sweep with their status moves. Walls to have to be wary of Kommo-o using Taunt, however, and that can work in to its advantage.

Disruption: When Kommo-o wants to set up, it is very weak to disruption such as Encore and Haze and phazing moves such as Roar, if not running Soundproof, and Whirlwind. Additionally, foes can utilize Mirror Herb to copy its boosts.

movesets.name: Offensive Z-Move
movesets.description:
Kommo-o is an unorthodox wallbreaker and setup sweeper that can blow past certain team structures with ease while also providing its team with notable defensive utility thanks to its typing and ability. However, Kommo-o's terrible matchup versus the tier's common Fairy-types such as Clefable and Tapu Lele limits its utility and means it requires significant support to be a consistent choice. Clanging Scales combines with Kommonium Z to give Kommo-o access to Clangorous Soulblaze, a powerful Z-Move that also boosts all of Kommo-o's stats one stage and notably OHKOes Great Tusk and offensive Landorus-T after Stealth Rock. Close Combat is preferred for its power, notably OHKOing Heatran at +1 and improving damage rolls against Melmetal and Mega Diancie. Drain Punch, although much weaker, gives Kommo-o some form of recovery and can let it heal off damage it may have taken while setting up on Pokemon such as Ferrothorn. Flamethrower hits Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Mega Scizor, preventing them from reliably trading with Kommo-o. Kommo-o is a decent Stealth Rock setter, as it dissuades common entry hazard removers such as Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Landorus-T from directly switching into it thanks to its Z-Move. Taunt is another option that allows Kommo-o to shut down Pokemon like Toxapex, Gliscor, and Galarian Slowking that might try to stop it via status or Haze. Clangorous Soul lets Kommo-o set up boosts reliably against teams with a Fairy-type, although it still won't sweep them easily, as Fairy-types like Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Tapu Fini can still take Kommo-o's boosted moves fairly comfortably. Additionally, while setting up both boosts is potentially devastating, it is often difficult to do so and unnecessary in a lot of situations due to Kommo-o's power at +1 often being sufficient. The other two moves are therefore often preferred. Bulletproof is very useful against foes such as Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo variants lacking Make it Rain, since it lets Kommo-o effectively counter them, turning them into setup fodder.

Kommo-o's threatening nature lets it fit well on offensive teams that want to keep the pressure on while appreciating Kommo-o's ability to check Hisuian Samurott, Mega Charizard Y, and Heatran. Kommo-o struggles greatly against Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, Tapu Lele, and Clefable, as they easily block its Z-Move while not being appreciably threatened by its coverage moves. Teammates that can take advantage of these Fairy-types are therefore required. Steel-types like Gholdengo, Melmetal, and Corviknight can come in on these Fairy-types and make progress via exerting significant offensive pressure from the former two or pivoting out and gaining momentum with the latter. Gholdengo also assists Stealth Rock variants of Kommo-o by blocking Rapid Spin and Defog attempts from Terapagos, Tornadus-T, and Zapdos. Kommo-o in turn can switch into Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Heatran, which threaten these Steel-types. Frail wallbreakers and cleaners, such as Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele love Kommo-o providing defensive utility on top of keeping up the offensive pressure for its teammates. Taunt variants work especially well with these teammates, as Kommo-o becomes adept at breaking down defensive cores consisting of Pokemon such as Toxapex, Gliscor, and defensive Landorus-T for these faster teammates. Kommo-o's access to Stealth Rock is useful for these offensive teams, as they sometimes struggle to fit Stealth Rock setters elsewhere, and they don't mind Kommo-o's limited longevity preventing it from setting up Stealth Rock multiple times over the course of a longer game. It notably frees up a moveslot on teammates such as Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Landorus-T. Hyper offense teams can often afford the Clangorous Soul variant of this set, as they generally have a dedicated lead devoted to setting entry hazards up. Teammates such as Iron Valiant, Roaring Moon, and Kingambit often fit on these teams and can pair with Kommo-o to exert immense offensive pressure on the opposing team and beat down their shared checks such as Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Toxapex.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Kommo-o is a unique Stealth Rock setter and special wall. Its Dragon typing combined with Bulletproof allows it to withstand hits from powerful attackers such as Mega Charizard Y, Ogerpon-W, and Volcarona, making it a solid check to all of them, as well as Gholdengo variants lacking Make It Rain. Body Press enables Kommo-o to threaten immediate damage on its targets such as Ogerpon-W and Serperior, as well as mauling Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Heatran. Toxic lets Kommo-o threaten common Body Press answers, notably Moltres, Tapu Lele, Zapdos, and Landorus-T. Stealth Rock allows Kommo-o to make long-term progress and enables the breakdown of many common offensive pieces, especially the 4x Rock-weak Mega Charizard Y and Buginium Z Volcarona. Protect lets Kommo-o recover HP for free with Leftovers, force foes to take an additional turn of poison damage, and scout threatening moves from Choice-locked Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Choice Specs Iron Valiant. Earthquake enables Kommo-o to not get stonewalled by Gholdengo, as well as threatening Galarian Slowking, Clodsire, and Tapu Koko. 32 Defense EVs with an Impish nature let Kommo-o take Mega Lopunny's Close Combat twice from full HP after Stealth Rock damage. 52 Speed EVs allow Kommo-o to outspeed uninvested Landorus-T, and 176 Special Defense EVs allow it to survive a Luster Purge from Mega Latios at full HP.

Kommo-o fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that can give it the specific support it needs to thrive. It can stave off offensive Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W, but it generally thuds against more defensive builds featuring Toxapex and Gliscor. Conversely, Kommo-o can be overwhelmed defensively by the threats it checks due to its lack of reliable recovery, so it requires a strong backbone and partners that it can rely on to cover its most glaring weaknesses, notably Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant and Hatterene. For this reason, Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo are excellent partners. Offensively, the ability to break past defensive pieces with Future Sight and Nasty Plot,respectively, gives teams a way to threaten the Toxic-immune Toxapex and Pecharunt, and Kommo-o can in turn serve to step in versus the Dark-types that force out both its teammates such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott. Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo also patch up the weakness to Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokemon, most notably Tapu Lele and Mega Latios. In a similar vein, Clefable helps against Dragon-types, serving to deny Garchomp and Dragonite the ability to obliterate Kommo-o with their powerful Z-Moves. Clefable can use Thunder Wave to make the Speed tiers of threatening sweepers like Ogerpon-W and Kartana more manageable for Kommo-o, and it can use Knock Off to remove the Heavy-Duty Boots that ignore Kommo-o's Stealth Rock. In turn, Kommo-o can deny the otherwise troublesome Ogerpon-W and Mega Charizard Y the opportunity to break through Clefable's otherwise robust defensive profile.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper (Fighting)
movesets.description: An incredible asset for Fighting teams, Kommo-o is often the best wincon on the type thanks to Clangorous Soulblaze, which helps it overcome otherwise difficult matchups such as Dragon, Flying, and Water. Flamethrower takes care of Steel-type Pokemon neutral to Drain Punch like Mega Scizor and Corviknight. Taunt allows Kommo-o to block status moves from defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Swampert, and Gliscor, preventing them from resetting its boosts with Haze or statusing it with Toxic. Alternatively, Clangorous Soul powers up Kommo-o without using its Z-Move, letting its Clangorous Soulblaze outright OHKO Toxapex and Hippowdon, at the cost of longevity. Bulletproof is Kommo-o's preferred ability to better handle Gholdengo or Aegislash in the Steel matchup. Unboosted Kommo-o's average Speed tier leaves it outsped by threats to Fighting teams like Tornadus-T and Tapu Lele, so Choice Scarf users like Galarian Zapdos and Terrakion are great partners to assist it against them. Iron Valiant's Fairy typing and wide coverage movepool lets it deal with opposing Dragon-types, and it forms a wallbreaking core with Kommo-o by pressuring the likes of Mega Sableye and Ting-Lu. Cobalion and Great Tusk provide Stealth Rock, which maximizes Kommo-o's opportunities to wallbreak after using Clangorous Soulblaze. Great Tusk can also remove entry hazards for Kommo-o with Rapid Spin, and Cobalion has the added bonus of checking Fairy-types like Mega Diancie. Mega Gallade can pressure Poison-, Ground-, and Flying-types like Toxapex, Ting-Lu, and Landorus-T for Kommo-o. It can also outspeed and revenge kill offensive threats to it like Kyurem and Garchomp.

movesets.name: Mixed Omni-Boost Sweeper (Dragon)
movesets.description: Kommo-o is an exceptional setup sweeper due to its great mixed offensive stats, respectable defenses, and exclusive access to Clangorous Soulblaze; this makes it an amazing tool to clean up Steel, Dark, and Dragon teams late-game. Drain Punch threatens Steel- and Normal-types like Heatran, Blissey, and Porygon-2 as well as increasing Kommo-o's longevity, making it harder for revenge killers to shut it down after using its Z-Move. Additionally, Drain Punch is Kommo-o's best move to hit Ditto, as it copies its ability Soundproof. Flamethrower targets Fighting-resistant or -immune Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Celesteela, and Aegislash. Taunt is preferred to shut down phazers like Haze Toxapex and Hippowdon and bulky walls like Porygon2 and Clodsire, which can inconvenience Kommo-o with Toxic. Meanwhile, Clangorous Soul allows for more boosts and breaking power, notably enabling Clangorous Soulblaze to OHKO the aforementioned Hippowdon and Toxapex. Furthermore, Clangorous Soulblaze allows Kommo-o to set up on Fairy-types and Soundproof Pokemon like Alolan Ninetales, Trace Porygon2, and opposing Kommo-o. Soundproof prevents revenge killing attempts from Ditto or opposing Kommo-o, and a Naive nature permits Kommo-o to outpace Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Lopunny, and Zeraora after obtaining the omni-boost. Mega Altaria is a wonderful teammate, as it helps weaken and clean up opposing Dragon teams; In return, it appreciates Kommo-o dealing with the aforementioned Steel-types. Kyurem aids in matchups against Flying-types like Tornadus-T, Mantine, and Dragonite, as well as Fairy-types such as Azumarill, Tapu Fini, and Mega Altaria. Choice Scarf Latias and Roaring Moon provide speed control; the former offers healing and setup opportunities with Healing Wish, while the latter checks Psychic-types like Deoxys-S, Victini, and Latias. Garchomp offers entry hazards support to pressure and chip down Kommo-o's switch-ins and aids in the Steel matchup with Earthquake. Hisuian Goodra is a huge help in the Fairy matchup, taking on Tapu Lele, Iron Valiant, and Mega Diancie. Mega Latios threatens Flying-type threats with its BoltBeam coverage; in addition, when paired with Garchomp, it puts a lot of pressure on Poison teams, which Kommo-o tends to struggle against. Cyclizar provides entry hazard control with Rapid Spin and extra protection for Kommo-o with Shed Tail, encouraging the use of Clangorous Soul over Taunt. Baxcalibur is excellent in the Dark and Flying matchups, dispatching threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Enamorus with its Swords Dance or Dragon Dance set, and it also ravages Poison teams with Galarian Slowking, which Kommo-o might not be able to handle. In return, Kommo-o removes the aforementioned Steel- and Normal-types that can easily wall Baxcalibur or use it to reverse sweep, specifically Ditto.
